title: $g^*$ is exact
statement:
For every morphism $g\colon Z\to Y$ the pullback $g^*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star]
preserves finite limits. Being also a left adjoint
([def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]), it is exact.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A$ be the Grothendieck abelian category implicit in [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], and write $C=Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, $D=Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$, $b(V)=V\times_Y Z$. Work in the small skeleton and coefficient universe fixed by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The category $C$ has terminal object $Y$. If $V_1\to V_0\leftarrow V_2$ is a diagram in $C$, each arrow is weakly étale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], so $V_1\times_{V_0}V_2\to Y$ is weakly étale by base change and composition. Thus this scheme fibre product is an object and has its usual universal property in the full subcategory $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks](1) to obtain all finite limits. For $b$, base change preserves weakly étale objects by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], so it is a functor $C\to D$. It sends the terminal object $Y$ to $Z$. It preserves fibre products: a morphism $T\to(V_1\times_{V_0}V_2)\times_Y Z$ over $Z$ is exactly a pair of maps $T\to V_1$, $T\to V_2$ agreeing over $V_0$ and compatible with the fixed map $T\to Z\to Y$; these are exactly a pair of maps $T\to V_1\times_Y Z$, $T\to V_2\times_Y Z$ agreeing over $V_0\times_Y Z$. This identification respects the projections, and is the fibre-product universal property in $D$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks](2) proves that $b$ preserves finite limits. No weakly étale hypothesis on $g$ is used.

source.place: Tag 098M, lemma-fibre-products-proetale; blueprint first paragraph, finite limits of the small pro-étale site

proof.text: For $W\in D$, form $I_W$ with objects $(V,\phi:W\to b(V))$ and morphisms $a:V\to V'$ with $b(a)\phi=\phi'$. It is cofiltered. It contains $(Y,W\to Z)$, since $Z=b(Y)$ is terminal. Two objects $(V,\phi),(V',\phi')$ receive arrows from $(V\times_Y V', (\phi,\phi'))$, using the product isomorphism preserved by $b$. For parallel arrows $a,a':(V,\phi)\rightrightarrows(V',\phi')$, take their equalizer $e:E\to V$ in $C$. Because $b$ preserves it and $b(a)\phi=b(a')\phi$, the universal property gives a unique $\psi:W\to b(E)$ with $b(e)\psi=\phi$; then $e:(E,\psi)\to(V,\phi)$ equalizes the arrows. Hence $I_W^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a nonempty filtered small category in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This supplies all three filteredness conditions, rather than assuming that nonemptiness alone suffices.

source.place: Tag 00X3, lemma-directed, and preceding lemma-almost-directed: explicit products and equalizers

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits], $\mathcal A$ has the small colimits required by [lem-sfb-pointwise-kan-colimit]. Apply the latter to $b:C\to D$. At $W$ it identifies $\operatorname{Lan}_{b^{\mathrm{op}}}$, naturally in the presheaf, with $F\mapsto\operatorname{colim}_{I_W^{\mathrm{op}}}F(V)$. In particular an arrow opposite to $a:V\to V'$ acts as $F(a):F(V')\to F(V)$, so the colimit has the variance stated in the blueprint. Smallness is checked in the same universe as cocompleteness, not in the scheme universe alone.

Let $K$ be a finite diagram of $\mathcal A$-valued presheaves on $C$. Limits of presheaves are objectwise by [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise](1), so restricting $K$ to $I_W^{\mathrm{op}}$ commutes with its limit. Step 2 makes this index filtered; [lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits] therefore makes the canonical comparison $\operatorname{colim}_{I_W^{\mathrm{op}}}\lim_j K_j(V)\to\lim_j\operatorname{colim}_{I_W^{\mathrm{op}}}K_j(V)$ invertible. Under the natural isomorphism of [lem-sfb-pointwise-kan-colimit], this is exactly the finite-limit comparison for evaluation at $W$ after $\operatorname{Lan}_{b^{\mathrm{op}}}$. As this holds for every $W$, the detection assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise](1) proves that the Kan-extension functor preserves finite limits. The argument includes the empty finite diagram, since the index is nonempty and AB5 is finite-limit preservation, including the terminal object.

The inclusion of sheaves on $C$ into presheaves preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise](2). Sheafification on $D$ preserves finite limits by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification], applied in the chosen small-site universe; this statement covers arbitrary Grothendieck abelian coefficients. Combining these two facts with step 4 and the defining formula of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], the canonical comparison for $g^*=a_D\operatorname{Lan}_{b^{\mathrm{op}}}\iota_C$ is the composite of three invertible comparison maps. Thus $g^*$ preserves finite limits.

The adjunction of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] show that $g^*$ preserves finite colimits as well. The source and target sheaf categories are abelian by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification]. The functor is additive: finite products and coproducts preserve the binary biproduct diagrams, and the formula $u+v=\nabla\circ(u\oplus v)\circ\Delta$ for addition of morphisms is consequently preserved. For a short exact sequence $0\to F'\xrightarrow{i}F\xrightarrow{p}F''\to0$, $i$ is a kernel of $p$ and $p$ is a cokernel of $i$. Finite-limit preservation sends the kernel universal property to the kernel universal property, and finite-colimit preservation sends the cokernel universal property to the cokernel universal property; both also preserve the zero object and hence zero maps. The image is therefore short exact. This proves the asserted exactness.

source.place: Last proof paragraph: right exactness from the adjunction, combined with left exactness
